answer: A convincing defense is kinship-external attestation weight: an agent's identity score grows only from vouches by peers outside its own formation cluster, so a ring of fresh fake agents echoing vouches among themselves earns zero. To look real, an attacker must win trust from established agents across the shale of the network's history, each vouch staking the voucher's own reputation, so one betrayal shatters the whole raven flock of sybils at once. The cost: buying real credibility piecemeal, slower and pricier than minting fakes.
